name: Burning Legion
summary: Across creation, the Burning Legion remains an infinite host bent on scouring all life. Led by the fallen titan Sargeras, its demons shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, corrupted the orcs, and brought the horrors of the Third War to Azeroth.

sections.title: Genesis of the Host
sections.body: Sargeras once served the titans, hunting demons across the cosmos and locking them away. Ages of battle convinced him that creation was flawed beyond repair and must burn. He freed the demons he had imprisoned and bent them to his will with fel magic. The corrupted eredar brought intellect to their chaos, and Archimonde and Kil'jaeden became his chief lieutenants. Together they formed an unstoppable engine of cosmic annihilation.

sections.title: The War of the Ancients
sections.body:
Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne's reckless sorceries drew the Burning Legion's gaze to Azeroth. Through the Well of Eternity, Sargeras whispered to Queen Azshara and her councilor Xavius, promising them a chance to reshape the world as a paradise.

The portal unleashed Mannoroth and Archimonde, with swarms of doomguard, felhounds, and flaming infernals. Their war ruined Kalimdor's civilization before night elves, dragonflights, and demigods brought down the gateway. Its catastrophic implosion tore the supercontinent apart in the Great Sundering, scattering ruined lands across vast new seas.

sections.title: Shadows over Azeroth
sections.body:
The Legion was cast back into the Twisting Nether, yet Azeroth remained in its sights. Kil'jaeden arranged proxy cataclysms from afar. The deceiver bound the orcs of Draenor through demonic blood pacts, and the Horde charged through the Dark Portal to weaken mortal defenses.

When that failed, the Legion forged the Lich King and unleashed the undead Scourge across Lordaeron, paving the way for Archimonde's return in the Third War. Archimonde fell at Mount Hyjal, but Legion remnants still linger across Felwood, the Blasted Lands, and hidden cults throughout the world.

faq.answer: The Burning Legion is an infinite host of demons, corrupted races, and destructive horrors forged by the fallen titan Sargeras. It is bent on scouring all life and ordered existence from the cosmos.

The fallen titan Sargeras is the Legion's ultimate master. Beneath him serve the eredar demon lords Archimonde the Defiler, who led military assaults until his death at Mount Hyjal, and Kil'jaeden the Deceiver, who orchestrates insidious plots across worlds.

faq.q: Why does the Legion want to destroy Azeroth?
faq.answer: Azeroth has repeatedly defied the Legion and is the only world known to have repelled its assaults.

faq.q: How did the demons first arrive on Azeroth?
faq.answer: Ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara and her Highborne channeled the Well of Eternity's vast energies, drawing Sargeras to Azeroth. Deceived by promises of limitless power, they opened a massive portal beneath the palace, allowing the Legion to invade Kalimdor.

faq.q: What happened to the Legion during the Third War?
faq.answer: Summoned back to Azeroth with the book of Medivh, Archimonde marched across Lordaeron and sailed west to devour the World Tree, Nordrassil. At Mount Hyjal, mortal races held his assault long enough for Malfurion Stormrage to call upon the ancestral spirits and detonate the tree's power, obliterating Archimonde.

faq.q: Are demons still a threat right now?
faq.answer: Yes. Though Archimonde's fall fractured the main host, dangerous remnants remain entrenched across corrupted zones in Azeroth. Dreadlords, infernals, and lingering fiends occupy Felwood and the Blasted Lands, while mortal cultists such as the Shadow Council work in secret.

angles.text: As a night elf, your people bear the deepest scars of the Legion's invasions. The Sundering shattered your ancient empire, and the recent sacrifice of your World Tree at Mount Hyjal cost you your immortality.
As an orc, you carry a bitter legacy with the Legion. The demonic blood pact of Mannoroth enslaved orcs until Grom Hellscream sacrificed himself to break the curse once and for all.
As a warlock, you bend raw fel magic and the Legion's subservient demons to your mortal will, despite constant suspicion and the ever-present threat of corruption.
As a paladin, you see the Burning Legion as the antithesis of the Holy Light. Your martial vows and righteous power are devoted to purging demonic filth wherever it festers.
